learner_operation: Inspect normalized y dependence in each equation and select exactly the equations with a linear y term and a distinct power term; nonpower dependence is disqualifying in these examples.

fixed_features.feature: Three equations with radio or Boolean checkbox subset response
fixed_features.justification: Preserves observed workload and source response banks.

fixed_features.feature: Nonpower distractor within its recognizable template
fixed_features.justification: sin(y), cos(y), or log(y) is mathematically decisive evidence that the learner must recognize; changing its truth would require replacing the obstruction, not merely varying an incidental assignment.

fixed_features.feature: Derivative multiplier fixed within each profile
fixed_features.justification: Preserves easy recognition versus moderate normalization workload; pure-power term exponents still change truth after division.

fixed_features.feature: Source x-function families and nonzero scalar range 1 through 5
fixed_features.justification: Coefficient recognition is ancillary; modest scalars preserve scope while answer-bearing y-exponent assignments vary.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Normalized linear y exponent can be present or absent independently subject to complete source radio bank.
answer_roles.observed: Every eligible row takes true and false roles across all feasible supported decision states.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: None/one/two/three as the source response bank and mathematical backbone permit.
answer_roles.observed: All feasible cases covered; None is explicit and keyed by negation of ordinary truth.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Not intrinsically correct; no fixed complete subset should follow from template labels alone.
answer_roles.observed: Best constant full response fails within every template and both exact-batch template subgroups; UI radio answer choices are shuffled.

coverage.case: Exact five-item runner batch after normalization/deduplication
coverage.result: All five survive; two q-108912 decisions and two q-108913 decisions (one repeated) remain, so neither subgroup has a constant full response.

counterfactuals.change: Change only the decisive left y exponent in one equation; hold all coefficients, other equations, and template fixed.
counterfactuals.expected: Exactly that equation changes truth, key/subset and explanation; old Boolean/subset value is rejected and new value accepted.
counterfactuals.observed: Eight template pairs pass prompt-row comparison, independent parsed math, explanation identity checks, and every-option native grading. Easy checkbox and moderate radio pairs rendered and screenshots inspected.
counterfactuals.justification: Presence of normalized y exponent 1 is essential evidence in the source classification.

counterfactuals.change: Alter only right-side nonzero x-only scalar in the same base equation.
counterfactuals.expected: Classification and Boolean/subset response preserved; changed coefficient appears in prompt and applicable solution.
counterfactuals.observed: All eight pairs preserve the response and retain valid worked content (generic nonexample explanations may stay identical); parsed exact identities and native grading pass. First and last template triples rendered.
counterfactuals.justification: Multiplying the nonzero power/nonpower term by an x-only constant does not change its dependence on y.

shortcut_probes.cue: sin(y), cos(y), or log(y) obstructs a single power
shortcut_probes.subgroup: Rows whose normalized nonderivative expression is a nonpower of y
shortcut_probes.strategy: Reject the nonpower row
shortcut_probes.conclusion: One fixed nonpower row in each of these templates is always false. Baseline is a random Boolean for that row. This predictor is the assessed y-dependence test itself, not an incidental label cue. Other pure-power rows change truth and determine different full responses.

stages_examined: shared publication normalization and inventory/within-batch deduplication
learner freshness and difficulty-first selection algorithm
delivery.result: 68/68 easy control records, 42/42 moderate controls and exact batch 5/5 survive with decision counts preserved. Conditional easy-band selection reaches every new record; actual policy/history unavailable and limits are stated in delivery-selection.json.

limitations: Finite tests do not prove absence of every shortcut.
Two unrated drafts and canonical record have incomplete essential replay evidence; they are explicitly distinguished from eight complete supported source families.
Historical inventory generation metadata is not captured; empty affected inventory means no demonstrated current finding matched, not verified absence of all historical defects.
Selection simulation uses specified history/weight scenarios and synthetic IDs, not a live learner snapshot.
